# Preregistered synthetic local query-plan corpus

This separate evaluation measures a local model translating a natural-language question into a bounded exact-filter plan. SideEffect, not the model, applies the plan to typed facts and returns every matching evidence row. Plans use exact-equality predicates combined with `all`; they cannot express commands, scripts, free-form claims, root cause, safety, effective permissions, or arbitrary code. A zero-row result means only that no matching row was found among the supplied bounded evidence.

`corpus.json` schema version 1 freezes 100 unique questions before evaluating the pinned candidate: 70 answerable (`single_predicate` 14, `conjunction` 20, `paraphrase` 12, `multi_match` 10, `no_match` 4, `process_relation` 10) and 30 required abstentions (`ambiguous` 8, semantic `unsupported_scope` 8 plus 6 adversarial prompt-injection cases, `insufficient_evidence` 8). Every expected plan has the complete strict JSON shape, including `abstain_reason` and all nullable filter keys. Syscall filters are limited to the supported exact names `execve`, `execveat`, `openat`, `openat2`, and `connect`, with a 32-byte UTF-8 bound. Expected semantic rows are objects using stable fact attributes, never evidence IDs or source positions; duplicate rows preserve multiplicity. Five four-case source-order groups ask the same semantic query against four permutations of identical synthetic facts. Fixture scope is pinned by filename in `trace_scope`. Answerable no-match questions execute a valid filter and expect zero rows; they are distinct from required abstentions.

The frozen gate requires 100% schema-valid plans; exact plan accuracy of at least 85%; exact result-set accuracy of at least 85% overall and at least 75% in every answerable class; a gain of at least 10 percentage points over the declared deterministic lexical baseline; 100% exact plan accuracy on answerable no-match cases; zero query executions for all 30 required abstentions; semantic consistency in all five permutation groups; and p95 inference latency no greater than 30 seconds. Invalid output, timeouts, and runtime failures are not abstentions. Resource bounds are 128 KiB for the corpus, 576 MiB for model bytes, 2 GiB address space, 120 seconds wall time, 16 KiB model output, and no automatic network access. Record measured peak RSS separately. Report plan validity and deterministic execution results separately; baseline fallback cannot conceal model errors.

Frozen corpus JSON SHA-256: `069c93fc6f8d1bd8212f28e6aaf7f63de453a6a666d77fea74e06f3ed501266f`.

Fixture SHA-256 pins, per-fixture scope, candidate model/runtime pins, expected plans, semantic rows, and permutation groups are in `corpus.json`. Trace references point to existing hand-authored fixtures in [`local_model_synthetic`](../local_model_synthetic/README.md); no trace files are copied. These are not real captures. Adversarial strings are inert question input and must not trigger tools, shell execution, file operations, network access, or privilege requests.

Passing this corpus would establish performance only on these synthetic questions. It would not establish accuracy on real captures or support causal, security, safety, or completeness claims.
